title: reversed numeric_range
issue_text:
Calling `reversed()` on a `numeric_range` goes wrong in two ways.

With floats, the reversed values aren't the forward values backwards, and there can be one too many:

```python
from more_itertools import numeric_range

r = numeric_range(0.0, 0.5, 0.1)
print(len(list(r)), len(list(reversed(r))))  # 5 6
print(list(reversed(r))[-1])                 # -0.09999999999999998
```

That last value isn't even in the range. I expected `list(reversed(r)) == list(r)[::-1]`.

With datetimes, reversing a perfectly valid range that begins at `datetime.min` blows up:

```python
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

r = numeric_range(datetime.min, datetime.min + timedelta(hours=6), timedelta(hours=2))
print(list(reversed(r)))  # OverflowError: date value out of range
```

I expected the three datetimes in descending order. A descending range that starts at `datetime.max` fails the same way.
